'''''Dangerous Dreams''''' was a compilation release by the [[Band/Legends|band]] [[Red Shift Limit/Legends|Red Shift Limit]], a member-alternating extension of a renegade underground [[Unidentified holo network|holo network]]. The release contained the tracks "[[Binary Cantata]]," "[[Dangerous Dreams (song)|Dangerous Dreams]]," "[[Imperial City (song)|Imperial City]]," and "[[Lost Voices]]." The cover art of the compilation featured the band and album's name in [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic]] and an oozing [[Eye/Legends|eye]] with a [[Bone/Legends|skull]] in its pupil.<ref name="GG9" /> It was available between the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="GG9date" />

At some point no later than [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="GG9date">''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]'' is set in the aftermath of the destruction of the first [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], but before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Per ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', the [[Time/Legends|time]] directly following the destruction occurs in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], and the battle occurs in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. Therefore, ''Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim'' is set from 0 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|ABY]] to 4 ABY.</ref> Dangerous Dreams was reviewed and banned by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Board of Culture]], as it was deemed to carry anti-Imperial sentiment.<ref name="GG9" />

==Behind the scenes==
''Dangerous Dreams'' was mentioned in [[1993]]'s ''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]'', a [[Galaxy Guide]] written by [[Simon Smith]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]] for [[West End Games]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. The book was illustrated by [[Mike Vilardi]].<ref name="GG9" />
